checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: The opening magenta-bar imagery and later texture (the pink wall AI, the badge colors, the crane-arm firefight, Boiler's tactile relationship to structures) genuinely seduce, but the piece is dominated by dense operational plotting — payment tallies, timelines, network layers — that keeps pulling focus back to procedure rather than sensory allure once the extraction begins.
checks.Fix: Trim some of the mid-to-late logistics exposition (the escrow mechanics, the multiple client-reveal justifications) and replace it with more sustained sensory/strange-beautiful GLMZ texture like the opening magenta-bar passage, so seduction persists past the first scene instead of yielding almost entirely to plot machinery.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The story opens directly on plot-critical action — Rook watching a bar, immediately followed by a client meeting where a five-person extraction job is pitched — with no grounded, plotless entry beat of someone simply moving through the city before the machinery engages.
checks.Fix: Precede the Gault meeting with a short beat of Rook navigating an ordinary piece of the city (a commute, a transaction, a routine errand) where the world's texture is felt before any job talk begins.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Most terms (Reibo flechette pistol, Greymark Unseen, Level IV fabrication suite, Casque & Veil integration layer) get an efficient in-voice gloss, but 'CorpoNations' itself is never actually glossed on first use — it appears only later ('outside CorpoNation jurisdiction') assuming the reader already parses it as a governing bureaucratic entity, and 'Z3/Z5/GLMZ' zone geography is deployed dozens of times before any orienting cue beyond 'the usual Z3 pretension' and 'the real GLMZ' — a phrase that gestures at insider contrast without telling a newcomer what tier or hierarchy these zones represent.
checks.Fix: Add one grounding clause early — e.g. when Rook first crosses zone lines — that lets a newcomer infer the Z-numbering is a wealth/security gradient across the GLMZ sprawl, phrased as her own habitual read of a block rather than as narration stepping outside her voice.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: 'GLMZ' appears repeatedly (e.g., 'This was the real GLMZ' and 'every biochemist in the GLMZ') with no in-voice expansion anywhere in the text; similarly 'ISB' is used ('ISB regulatory compliance,' 'the 2218 Infrastructure Safety Mandate') though 'Infrastructure Safety Bureau' is given before it, GLMZ never gets that treatment.
checks.Fix: Add an in-voice gloss the first time 'GLMZ' appears, e.g. 'the Greater Lake Metro Zone, GLMZ to anyone who'd lived here more than a week,' before using the bare acronym thereafter.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The scene at the diner where Rook counts the cash but privately fixates on 'the woman she hadn't brought and couldn't stop seeing' — and earlier, saying Wennick's name aloud 'for the first time in three years' to Vox — gives a controlled but genuine crack: grief and guilt surfacing through the armor of competence.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The ending does land a quiet final gesture — Rook 'let the count stay one short,' pocketing the money while refusing to close the ledger on the Bloom Quarter woman — but it's buried under paragraphs of plot-resolution accounting (Vox's market summary, Adalemo's status, escrow receipt) that read as epilogue-tidying rather than a single held beat, and the closing lines ('the list that was four names and still had room for more... she made herself stop looking') tip toward a hopeful/forward-looking note rather than pure weight.
checks.Fix: Cut the market-summary and status-update paragraphs entirely and end on the unresolved count — the coffee cup, the twelve francs, the lake — without the coda about the crew list and 'next time,' so the last image is the cost she's carrying rather than a gesture toward future jobs.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The magenta motif (Axiom's ad wash) is planted purely as scene color on first read, but retroactively colors the entire betrayal — the bar 'running magenta' before Rook even knows Axiom is involved, and later the compound wearing 'the brand the way the brand wanted to be worn' pays off differently once the reader knows Ohara has been steering events from inside that color scheme for fourteen months. Similarly, Rook's habitual door-counting and the Wennick references work as pure characterization on a first pass but reread as direct foreshadowing of the climactic choice to look back at Gault and to hang from a departing skid rather than let a door fail someone again.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose reads as a fully-realized standalone thriller with its own complete arc (job → betrayal → storm finale → resolution), and worldbuilding terms like 'Z3/Z5', 'neuretics', 'Ghost/Husk/Shell', and 'PEREGRINE' are consistently explained in-line at first use (e.g. 'The thing nobody outside the trade understood about Ghosts was the cost of admission...') rather than assuming prior familiarity.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: The story braids all five pillars into functioning texture: Okafor and Vox running AI agents with personality and stakes ('The wall believed it knew what noise looked like'), nanites as everyday economy and body-repair infrastructure (Ohara's formula literally encoded in her neural substrate, the F8,400 Axiom treatment ad), neuretics stratifying competence and cost (Diallo's commercial Atlas-grade vs. Vox's archology-tier 'visible was the point', Okafor's bandwidth-driven detachment), CorpoNations as the real law with PEREGRINE as their extralegal enforcement arm operating beyond any police (since dissolved), and gray zones like the Bloom Quarter and the Lake Platform's Meridian Charter waters existing explicitly outside CorpoNation jurisdiction.
checks.Fix: The Schism itself is never mentioned even obliquely — no reference to reality-warping aftermath, physics anomalies, or the rift as a lived environmental/historical fact, so a cold reader gets four pillars solidly but could finish the story without sensing the Schism exists at all.
